objective: Defining sustainability, regeneration, and resilience in project environments: reducing negative environmental impact and designing projects to withstand or recover from extreme events
secondaryObjectives: Explaining the Triple Bottom Line: People, Planet, and Prosperity considerations

sources.cite: PMI, Certified Sustainable Project Professional (CSPP) bundle and exam page: P5 Standard: Sustainability and Impact Analysis 24% (the largest domain with PRiSM Life Cycle Approach 23% and Project Management Considerations 23%)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 directly (summarizing fetch of pmi.org/certifications/cspp-bundle-exam-course). The page lists six domains: Foundations of Sustainable Project Work 12%, PRiSM Life Cycle Approach 23%, P5 Standard: Sustainability and Impact Analysis 24%, Developing a Sustainability Management Plan 12%, ESG & Sustainability Reporting, Governance, and Project Communications 7%, Project Management Considerations 23% (they add to 101%). It says the P5 Standard evaluates project impacts on 'people, planet, and prosperity', and a prep module practices 'a P5 Impact Analysis' to 'identify, assess and mitigate sustainability impacts'. The course seed's five domains and weights (P5 36%) differ from this page; the P5 domain is the largest either way. The objective wording is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's cspp-school-laptop-p5-review (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the project, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You manage the build of a rural health clinic for a fictional district health board. The site is in a 1-in-50-year flood zone; the brief says 'sustainable building'.
handover: The design team proposes a standard design with solar panels.
The last flood cut the road for four days.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each review; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

effects.finding: Floods reach 0.8 m on the site about once in 50 years; climate projections make it more frequent. The road floods first.

then.log: Week 2: the design review shows the clinic's ground floor and generator below the projected flood level; redesign costs 6 weeks.
Week 3: the national contractor wins on price; the promised local jobs don't appear and community trust drops.
Week 4: the flood model shows filling the wetland raises flood levels at neighboring homes; the council refuses consent.

resPrompt.title: What 'sustainable' means here
resPrompt.context: The design team offers solar panels.

choices.label: Set objectives for resilience (floor raised above the projected flood level, backup power and water for 5 days, access by an alternative route) alongside reduced impact
choices.feedback: Resilience means withstanding and recovering from extreme events; it belongs in the objectives.

choices.label: Accept the standard design with solar panels
choices.feedback: Lower impact, but the clinic floods.

choices.label: Treat the flood risk as an insurance matter
choices.feedback: Insurance pays after; the community loses its clinic when it needs it most.

tblPrompt.title: People, planet, prosperity
tblPrompt.context: A national contractor quotes 8% less than local firms.

choices.label: Weigh all three: local firms and apprentices (people, prosperity), lower transport emissions (planet), at an 8% premium the sponsor approves

effects.log: The sponsor approves the local approach.

choices.feedback: The triple bottom line weighs social, environmental and economic value together.

choices.label: Choose the cheapest bid
choices.feedback: Prosperity narrowly; people and planet ignored.

choices.label: Promise local jobs in the press without budget
choices.feedback: An unfunded commitment to the community.

regenPrompt.title: Leaving the site better
regenPrompt.context: Wetland on the site edge absorbs flood water.

choices.label: Restore and extend the wetland as natural flood storage, part of the landscaping budget
choices.feedback: Regeneration leaves systems better than before; here it also reduces flood risk.

choices.label: Leave the wetland as it is
Fill the wetland for parking
choices.feedback: Filling it removes flood storage and habitat.

reflection.question: Write the objectives record: what sustainable, resilient and regenerative mean for this clinic.

parts.label: Resilience and impact

parts.label: Value and regeneration
parts.criteria: Local firms and apprentices at an approved premium; wetland restored.
parts.modelAnswer: Local firms and apprentices build it at an 8% premium the sponsor approved; the wetland is restored as flood storage.

scoring.modelReasoning: Sustainability in projects covers reducing negative impact, resilience (designing to withstand and recover from extreme events) and regeneration (leaving systems better). The triple bottom line weighs people, planet and prosperity together rather than cost alone.
